  "partial_result": "**Decision: STOP.** Do not fund rank-32 LoRA on PE's six upper blocks, and do not spend a CPU job qualifying its mechanics. The parameter inventory below is enough to see the cost envelope without one.\n\n**Measured grounds.** The saved-state attribution locates PE's deficit as \"learns less from identical exposure\", not \"loses what it had\". Raw held R@1 moves from +3.86 to \u22120.65 points versus Large, mAP@R from +3.26 to \u22122.13, and every measured state improves monotonically for both arms. A rank constraint removes adaptable directions and, at matched steps, slows learning in function space. Its only route to a gain is over-adaptation damage, and no saved state shows any. The gap a LoRA arm would have to close is against dense PE at the same 100 updates:\n\n| Needed versus archived dense PE | Points |\n|---|---:|\n| R@1 to reach Large minus 0.5 | +0.10 |\n| mAP@R to reach Large minus 1.0 | +1.24 |\n\nThe published behaviour of LoRA at matched steps, in Hu et al. 2021 and Biderman et al. 2024, is to trail full fine-tuning on the target distribution. The pre-registered expectation for this arm is therefore a fail. Funding a near-certain STOP is not justified.\n\n**Why neither rank capture nor covariance can be a prerequisite.** The rank-32 receipt describes the endpoint of the unconstrained AdamW trajectory. A constrained learner does not approximate that endpoint. It optimizes the same loss over a different set, along a different Adam path, so the quality of its optimum is a property of the constrained problem, not of a projection of the dense solution. Frobenius capture is also neither necessary nor sufficient for retrieval: MLP hidden-unit permutations and head permutations are exact function invariances with nonzero Frobenius energy, while a rank-1 update along one discriminative direction can move retrieval a lot. Covariance statistics fail the same way. The signed 90-degree permutation from the displacement gate preserves every covariance eigenvalue and every dot product, so covariance cannot distinguish an update that matters from one that does not, and Adam's per-coordinate normalization decouples update directions from gradient covariance magnitude anyway. The only measurement that qualifies a LoRA arm is the held quality of the trained arm itself. Any cheaper threshold would be a fabricated licence.\n\n**What inference would survive if it were run anyway.** Only a procedure-level contrast: \"rank-32 LoRA procedure versus the archived dense procedure, same 100 batches, same RGB hashes, same initializers, same 6,354 query and 6,245 gallery roles\". One arm bundles the rank constraint, factor initialisation and scaling, Adam geometry on factors, decay location, and a factor learning rate that is a convention, not a calibration. Separating the rank constraint needs a full-rank factorised control at r = 768, costing 2 to 2.7 times the dense parameters per matrix and a second GPU arm, and it still leaves the factor learning rate free. Weight decay is the one confound that bounds cleanly:\n\n| Decoupled decay over 100 updates | Relative shrink |\n|---|---:|\n| Dense tail, lr 1e-5, wd 0.05 | 0.005% |\n| LoRA factors, lr 1e-4, wd 0.05 | 0.05% on factors, order 1e-6 on W |\n| Observed PE block updates | 0.107% to 0.256% |\n\nCost-matched claims are excluded by the no-extension rule, so only exposure-matched claims exist, and those are the ones expected to fail.\n\n**Inventory and mechanics, for the record.** From the authenticated trainable names, PE's six upper blocks hold four matrices each: fused attention in_proj 2304\u00d7768, out_proj 768\u00d7768, c_fc 3072\u00d7768, c_proj 768\u00d73072.\n\n| Group | PE blocks 6 to 11 | Large blocks 12 to 23 |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Dense matrices that LoRA would replace | 24, about 42.5M | 72, about 151.0M |\n| Rank-32 factors | about 2.36M | about 7.08M |\n| Still dense-trainable: norms, biases, pool, projection | about 7.9M | about 12.8M |\n\nThe fused in_proj is a bare parameter, so module wrapping would require editing native source. Parametrization through torch.nn.utils.parametrize applies to bare parameters and to proj uniformly, materializes W0 plus scaled BA under the same autocast cast that serving uses, and merging is remove_parametrizations with leave_parametrized, which restores the original 163 keys and shapes for the strict loader. With B zero-initialised the materialized weight is W0 plus exact zeros, so step-0 held vectors must match an unwrapped forward bitwise in the same process and dtype, and the cached fit matrix within the existing 0.999 floor. Merged versus training-time parity is tolerance-based only, using the existing golden-vector protocol of cosine at least 0.999999 and packed hits within 1e-6. If overridden, the frozen stop is the archived gate against the archived Large control at the point estimate, one PE arm, whole process under 300 seconds, allocated CUDA under 10 GB, host 8 GiB, shared lock, no retry. Dense PE peaked at 5.22 GB, and LoRA removes about 0.5 GB of gradients and moments.\n\n**Boundary of this STOP.** It closes rank-32 LoRA on PE's upper blocks as a quality-recovery intervention at matched exposure. It does not close adaptation in general. It leaves untested LoRA used as cheap prefix extension over all twelve PE blocks, which is a capacity and freeze-depth question with no measured support in the repository, and I do not propose it. No distinct supported mechanism follows from the saved-state attribution, so no alternative is recommended. No file was edited, no process launched, and no operator contact made.",
